title: How a Suspension Bridge Actually Stays Up

segments.text: This bridge spans over a mile, yet it looks like it's just hanging there.
How can these thin cables hold thousands of tons? It's simpler than you think.
First, giant anchors are buried deep into solid rock, gripping the main cables.
Then two huge towers rise up, carrying the entire weight of those cables.
From the main cables, thin vertical wires drop down and hold up the road.
The road deck isn't rigid. It flexes slightly, soaking up wind and traffic.
So the deck doesn't hold the cables. The cables hold the deck, perfectly balanced.
A quiet dance of tension and steel, turning thin wire into human connection.

description: How does a suspension bridge actually stay up? It's a brilliant balance of forces. Follow Curio for your daily dose of science 🔬
